verdict.reasoning: Patient states she is 26 years old and presents with headache for a few days: “I'm 26 year old” and “this… headache that's been going on for a few days… Around three days ago, maybe.”
Doctor clarifies onset: “Around three days ago, maybe.” / “Three days ago. Okay…”
Location described as mostly around right eye: “it kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly around my right eye.”
Nature described as dull with occasional sharpness: “It's kind of. It's dull, but sometimes it gets a bit sharper.”

Gradual worsening described: “it developed gradually… the first day it just started when I was at work and by the end of the day it was like… a lot… Then I woke up the next morning like it was even, even worse.”
Constant with fluctuating intensity: “It kind of comes and goes, but I mean, it is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger.”
Pain score documented: Doctor asks 1–10 scale; patient: “It's probably an 8.”
Initial shooting lights reported: “just when it started I got this like weird shooting lights.”
Photophobia described: “now like light is quite annoying my eyes.” and to clarification: “When you say annoying, does it hurt to look at bright lights?” Patient: “Yeah, yeah, it hurts.”
Nausea without vomiting: “Any nausea or any vomiting?” Patient: “Well, basically I'm sick with the headache, but I. No vomiting.” The feeling sick implies nausea with no vomiting.
No visual loss: “Any loss of vision or blurry vision?” Patient: “Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say.”
No neck stiffness: “Any neck pain or neck stiffness?” Patient: “No.”
No speech difficulty: “And any difficulty with speaking or speech?” Patient: “No.”
No limb weakness: “Any difficulty with weakness in your arms and legs?” Patient: “No.”

Ibuprofen use and dose: “So I tried ibuprofen. So I took like a few for the last two days, basically.” Later clarified: “How many tablets did you take of ibuprofen? … Three a day.” and it “doesn't really help.”
No personal history of migraine: “Any history of migraines at all?” Patient: “Not myself. I've never had a migraine, but my sister and my mum have them…”
Past headaches relieved by ibuprofen: “Yeah, I mean, I had, but usually after I take ibuprofen, it kind of goes away, so. But this time it's just not.”
Recent ibuprofen use at 3 tablets/day for 2 days, ineffective: “I tried ibuprofen… took like a few for the last two days… But it doesn't really help.” and “How many tablets…? … Three a day.”
No regular meds: “Before I go any further, can I ask, do you take any regular medication?” Patient: “No.”
Denies allergies: “Do you have any allergies to any medications?” Patient: “Not that I know of.”
Family history in mother and sister: “Any history of migraines at all?” Patient: “…my sister and my mum have them quite frequently.”
Mother’s severe migraines with season changes: “my mom's is like quite bad. Usually when there's like a season changing and stuff like that, it's. Yeah, takes her out for a few days, basically.”
Lives with three housemates: “I live with housemates, so three of them.”
Works in IT with heavy screen use: “Yeah, so I work well, I work in it, so I work with computers a lot, so it kind of is difficult to focus. I had to like reduce the brightness of my screen.”
Wears glasses and no recent eye test: “Do you wear glasses?” Patient: “Yes, I do.” and “Have you had a recent eye check done? Eye test?” Patient: “No, I've been wearing them since I was five.”

Occasional alcohol: “Regarding smoking or alcohol, do you drink or smoke at all?” Patient: “I socially smoke and I drink. Not only socially.” Doctor: “Only socially.” Although slightly ambiguous, her answer indicates non-heavy, situational drinking consistent with occasional alcohol use.
Social smoker: “I socially smoke and I drink.”

Doctor’s assessment of probable migraine based on history: “I do think this could be a headache very similar to migraine. The reason I say that is because the history is very suggestive of it. Given your mum and your sister also have migraines.” Symptoms of photophobia, nausea, typical headache features are described earlier in HPI.
Ibuprofen ineffective: “But it doesn't really help.” and later concern about dose: “Now, my only worry is I'm not sure whether you're taking the correct dose.”
Counseling on maximum ibuprofen dosing: “You try the ibuprofen. Now, my only worry is I'm not sure whether you're taking the correct dose. You can take up to two tablets three times a day.”
Consider naproxen: “Or I can prescribe you something stronger like naproxen, which is another anti inflammatory, which can be helpful.”
Consider codeine-containing analgesic: “We can also add in other painkillers like paracetamol or codeine, which might be helpful as well.” and “I can give you a prescription for that today.”
Headache diary advised: “With regards to the next few days, it may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's. If there's any triggers…”
Eye exam recommendation if eye strain: “if you feel like your eyes are straining, I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done.”

Follow-up in 1–2 weeks with consideration of prophylaxis: “I'd like you to come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time. If you are having more frequent episodes… we can think about giving you medications as prophylactic…”

Return sooner if worse or new neuro/vision symptoms: “if your headaches aren't getting any better or they're getting worse, you know, I want you to give me a call or come back and see me sooner… If you have any problems with your vision or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well, just give me a call and come back and see me.”
No vitals are mentioned anywhere in the transcript, so stating that none are documented is consistent with the record.
No physical examination findings (e.g., neuro exam, funduscopic, general exam) are described in the transcript, so it is accurate that none are documented.
